# r1 — Reachable

## What this measures

Can an AI agent's *fetcher* reach this site at all? Agent products fetch with
their own user-agents (ChatGPT-User, Claude-User, PerplexityBot,
OAI-SearchBot); a WAF that challenges or blocks those UAs closes the door
before any commerce protocol matters. This is the pre-flight: when it fails,
r2–r5 are scored **Blocked**, not Fail — fixing access is action #1.

Blocking *training* crawlers (GPTBot, CCBot) in robots.txt is a legitimate
policy choice and is not penalized. Blocking *fetchers* is what ends the
agentic commerce conversation.

## Sub-checks

| Sub-check | Pass when | Weight | Fix skill |
|-----------|-----------|-------:|-----------|
| browser baseline reachable | `GET /` with a browser UA → 200, no challenge interstitial | 1 | — |
| agent fetcher UAs served like a browser | Each fetcher UA gets 200, no challenge markers, body not <20% of baseline size | 3 | `webmcp-browser-agents:webmcp-setup` |
| robots.txt present | `GET /robots.txt` → 200, non-empty | 1 | — |
| robots.txt does not disallow agent fetchers | No `User-agent: <fetcher>` block with site-wide `Disallow: /` (a missing robots.txt disallows nothing, so it passes) | 2 | — |

## N/A condition

None — every site has an access surface.

## Fix guidance

Allow the agent/fetcher bot category in your WAF or CDN bot management
(Cloudflare: the "AI Agent" / verified-bots category is per-category since
mid-2025). Keep training-crawler policy separate from fetcher policy — they
are different robots.txt user-agents and different WAF categories.
